The structure is described in the monoclinic space group Cc, number 9, with Hall symbol C -2yc. The supplied input cell is primitive in shape but nonstandard in orientation relative to the conventional Cc setting. Its lattice parameters are a = 4.62245001 Å, b = 4.622450009999999 Å, c = 16.45451005 Å, with α = 89.87526837000001°, β = 89.87526837000001°, and γ = 103.63948624°. The declared input composition is Bi₂H₂Se₄O₁₂, corresponding to 20 atoms in the input cell.

Fractional coordinates are used throughout. The standard and input frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0). The transformation matrix P has first row (0.5, 0.5, 0.0), second row (0.5, -0.5, 0.0), and third row (2.1509286472177556e-20, 2.1509286472177556e-20, -0.9999999999999999). Thus the standard a axis is the sum of the input a and b directions, the standard b axis is their difference, and the standard c axis is essentially the reversed input c axis, with only negligible numerical components in the third row. This relation allows the original input cell to be recovered from the standard description.

All atoms occupy the general Wyckoff position 4a of Cc, with coordinate relation x, y, z and multiplicity four. Positional values are rounded to six decimal places before any listed correction. The independent sublattices are as follows.

Bismuth occupies one independent 4a orbit, with representative fractional position (0.22024500000000002, 0.22191000000000005, 0.9114109999999999). Hydrogen occupies one independent 4a orbit, represented by (0.2145485, 0.039077500000000015, 0.12611099999999992).

There are two crystallographically independent selenium orbits, both 4a. The first Se representative is (0.23275500000000005, 0.2424280000000001, 0.562554), and the second Se representative is (0.23276699999999995, 0.38141099999999994, 0.29476499999999994).

Oxygen occupies six independent 4a orbits. Their representative positions are (0.00459849999999995, 0.15356250000000005, 0.508823), (0.473186, 0.15452100000000002, 0.514342), (0.22837800000000003, 0.085893, 0.6488659999999999), (0.485721, 0.248987, 0.803673), (0.24887749999999986, 0.4801685, 0.3935519999999999), and (0.448824, 0.21809299999999998, 0.31209299999999995). Together, the fourfold repetition of these six oxygen orbits gives the twelve oxygen atoms of the input composition, while the single Bi orbit, single H orbit, and two Se orbits account for the remaining atoms.

One precision correction must be retained in the input geometry. An oxygen atom located before correction at fractional coordinates (0.729046, 0.768709, 0.606448) is displaced by (-9.999999999177334e-07, 0.0, 0.0). This is a very small shift in the x coordinate only, effectively a one-unit change in the sixth decimal place, and it preserves the real input geometry rather than forcing it onto an exactly idealized symmetry value.
